newsitem.title: UK: UK's Rifkind-Conservatives could join EMU in 2 yrs.
newsitem.headline: UK's Rifkind-Conservatives could join EMU in 2 yrs.

text.p: A British Conservative government could lead Britain into European Economic and Monetary Union in two years' time if it wins the general election next year, foreign secretary Malcolm Rifkind said on Friday.
"That is a possibility as the Chancellor of the Exchequer has explained," Rifkind told BBC radio.
He said it was possible for any British government to win a referendum on EMU and make the Bank of England independent within two years "if it was in the British national interest."
"But the electorate are going to have the final word on the question of a single currency," he added.

The Maastricht Treaty set a start date of January 1, 1999 for a single currency. "The option to join remains, that is the whole point of the opt-out," Rifkind said. "But we, unlike most other countries, are not committed to joining a single currency regardless of the circumstances."

Speaking at the start of a European Union summit on EMU in Dublin, Rifkind said the summit could see attempts to see early decisions pushed through. "I think that...the French government and one or two other delegations will try to force premature decisions on Europe. That is going to be resisted," he said.
Rifkind said some countries were prepared to give up their national veto in EU negotiations but few had nailed their colours to the mast on that issue.
"Either they are changing their mind when facing reality or they are keeping their powder dry until a later stage in the negotiation," Rifkind said.
